Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National President Mahama urges Ghanaians to invest in manufacturing Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 5:58pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Dramani Mahama has urged Ghanaian entrepreneurs and investors to shift their focus from trading to manufacturing, saying the country must build a strong industrial base by processing its raw materials into finished products.
He said Ghana had the resources and entrepreneurial capacity to establish factories that could manufacture goods for both local consumption and export, rather than depend heavily on imported products.
Speaking at the commissioning of EXIM Bank-funded NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026, President Mahama challenged Ghanaians to take advantage of opportunities in manufacturing and agro-processing.
“We must change that mindset. We are not a country of traders. We are a country of manufacturers,” he said.
The President argued that exporting raw agricultural produce deprived Ghana of employment opportunities and income that could otherwise be generated through local processing.
He cited the example of cashew, noting that Ghana had for years exported large quantities of the nuts with limited local processing.
He said his government was committed to reversing the trend by supporting the establishment and expansion of factories across the country.
“All these factories that are being built, Ghanaians can build them. They are Ghanaians who have the resources to be able to build them,” he said.
President Mahama stressed that Ghana needed to move beyond establishing factories that produce basic consumer goods and invest more in industries that process the country's agricultural and natural resources.
“We shouldn't only open pure water factories. We have enough pure water factories. We need factories that will process our raw materials for export. We need factories that will create jobs for our people,” he said.
He identified maize, rice and mangoes as some of the agricultural commodities with significant potential for local processing.
“I want to see more NADKANSCOs, not only processing cashew, but processing many other things. Processing maize flour, processing rice for local consumption and export, processing mangoes for juice for local consumption and export. There's so much that we can do,” he added.
The President said industrialisation was central to his government's new economy agenda, which seeks to create employment opportunities, particularly for young people, through investments in productive sectors.
He disclosed that government planned to invest $10 billion of its own resources in eight sectors expected to drive economic growth and job creation.
Agriculture and agribusiness, including the tree crops sector, are among the priority areas.
President Mahama said the government would continue to support businesses involved in manufacturing and agro-processing to strengthen domestic production, reduce reliance on imports and increase Ghana's export earnings.
